To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

UACR or hsCRP added to risk prediction by the HeartScore system changed risk classification in one-fifth, and that UACR and the combination of UACR, hsCRP or Nt-proBNR added to risk prediction of known cardiovascular disease or diabetes changed risk classification in another one-fifth of a Danish population sample.

in subjects with low risk of cardiovascular death (10-year risk below 5%) and no history of cardiovascular disease or diabetes, the use of additional risk markers (urine albumin/creatine ratio and high-sensitivity C reactive protein) changes the HeartScore risk category in 19% from low to high, and that in subjects with known cardiovascular disease or diabetes and no use of cardiovascular medication, the use of the additional markers urine albumin/creatine ratio and N-terminal pro-brained

the use of additional biomarkers, in particular albuminuria and hsCRP, may significantly change the HeartScore classification and risk stratification in a large proportion of the population, and this is particularly important in the group of patients with low-moderately increased risk.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of biomarkers to improve the risk classification of individuals with low-moderately increased risk and of individuals with diabetes or cardiovascular disease.
the development of a new risk classification system for cardiovascular risk prediction in subjects with low to moderate risk and in patients with known diabetes and cardiovascular disease.
the development of risk markers to improve cardiovascular risk prediction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
UACR, hsCRP and Nt-pro-BNP add to risk prediction based solely on HeartScore and presence of diabetes or cardiovascular history, but the added value is limited and depends on the clinical context.
the additional use of UACRs and/or hsCRP and/or Nt-proBNPs may change the Heart Score risk classification significantly in about 20% of the population.
UACR, hsCRP and Nt-pro-BNP add to risk prediction based upon HeartScore and history, but that the clinical value depends on the risk category and on the clinical context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in subjects with low to moderate cardiovascular risk and without history of diabetes or CVD, the addition of UACR or hsCRP to HeartScore may change risk classification in one-fifth and the addition of U-ACR and N-terminal pro-bran natriuretic protein (NT-proBNP) may change risk classification to one-fourth of the population.
in the general population, the use of UAC and hsCRP can improve the prediction of CEP, whereas the use of Nt-proBNPs does not seem to add much to the prediction.
the new markers add to the risk classification of HeartScore in one-fifth, but not all of the population.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the risk prediction based on the traditional Framingham risk factors may be improved by adding novel markers such as UACR or hsCRP in the low-moderated risk group and UACR, hsCRP or Nt-proBNR in the patient group.
a combination of UACR, hsCRP and Nt-pro-BNP can identify high-risk patients in whom the HeartScore classification would be low-moderate.
the addition of biomarkers to risk assessment based on HeartScore may identify a subgroup of subjects with a higher risk than predicted by HeartScore.
